text.en:
Establishment of Floor Price of Palay. The Department of
Agriculture (DA), upon consultation with the Steering Committee created under

hereof, shall determine, set, and adjust the floor price of palay to be
purchased by the government based on the following considerations:
a. Cost of production;
b. Prevailing market prices;
c. Reasonable margins for farmers;
d. Welfare of both farmers and consumers; and
e. Other relevant factors and conditions, such as:
i. Emergencies or calamities affecting the rice supply chain and palay
production;
il. Influx of import arrivals that could dampen farmgate price of palay;
ill. Sharp decline in global rice prices that may impact the estimated landed cost
iv. Government's capacity to purchase palay at competitive prices and manage
market intervention.
In establishing the floor price of palay, the DA shall ensure a fair return of
investment to farmers on a regional level by recognizing regional variance in
production costs, market conditions, and profit margin, to be reviewed and adiusted
before the onset of cropping season or whenever necessary.
Section 2. Steering Committee. A Steering Committee is hereby created to
assist the DA in establishing the floor price of palay and implementing this Order.
The Committee shall be composed of the heads of the following agencies:
Chairperson
Co-Chairperson
Department of the Interior and Local Government
Department of Trade and Industry;
Department of Social Welfare and Development;
Department of Agrarian Reform; and
National Food Authority (NFA)
2

The Committee may invite representatives from local government units
(LGUs), farmer representatives, private sector groups, and civil society organizations
as observers and/or resource persons to aid in the performance of the Committee's
The DA shall serve as the Secretariat of the Committee, and shall provide
administrative and technical support to the Committee.
The Chairperson, Co-Chairperson, and members of the Committee may
designate their respective alternates, with ranks not lower than Assistant Secretary
or its equivalent, who are fully authorized to decide for or on their behalf
The Committee shall regularly convene at least once every quarter or as often
as may be deemed necessary by the Chairperson.
The Steering Committee may request the assistance of other government
agencies and LGUs to provide timely assistance and cooperation to ensure the
effective and efficient implementation of this Order.

Temporary Storage of Palay in Public Facilities. In the absence
or insufficiency of available and suitable warehouses for the proper storage of
purchased palay, national government agencies (NGs) and instrumentalities,
including government -owned or -controlled corporations (GOCCs) and state
universities and colleges (SUCs), and LGUs shall be authorized to use public
facilities such as covered courts, multi-purpose halls, gymnasiums and other
governmentowned structures as temporary storage sites, subject to existing laws,
rules and regulations.
Such use shall be coordinated with the concerned LGUs and other relevant
government agencies to ensure that the storage of palay does not impede the
delivery of essential public services.

Sanctions. The purchase of palay by any NGA and LGU below
the floor price and any violation of this Order shall be referred to the proper
disciplining authority for administrative action, in accordance with relevant laws, rules
and regulations.

Implementing Guidelines. Within five (5) days from the effectivity
of this Order, the Steering Committee shall formulate the necessary guidelines for
the full and effective implementation of this Order. The Implementing Guidelines shall
include the proper utilization, maintenance, and security of temporary storage
facilities to prevent post-harvest losses and ensure the protection and quality of
stored palay, among others.

Monitoring. To ensure effective implementation of this Order, the
Steering Committee, shall conduct regular monitoring of farmgate transactions to
ensure that palay prices remain fair, stable, and beneficial to both farmers and
3

Reporting. The Steering Committee shall submit to the President,
through the Office of the Executive Secretary, quarterly reports on the status of
compliance, implementation progress, and the impact on farmer incomes and rice
supply stability.

Funding. The funding requirements for the initial implementation
of this Order shall be charged against the existing appropriations of concerned
agencies of the Steering Committee and such other funding sources as may be
identified by the Department of Budget and Management, subject to relevant
budgeting, accounting, and auditing laws, rules and regulations. Thereafter, the
subsequent funding requirements for the continued implementation of this Order
shall be included in the budget proposals of concerned agencies, subject to the
usual budget preparation process.

Transitory Clause. Upon effectivity of this Order, and pending the
issuance of the guidelines to be issued by the Steering Committee, the floor price of
palay shall be based on the current regional floor price computation of the NFA.

Separability. If any part or provision of this Order shall be held
unconstitutional or invalid, the other provisions not affected thereby shall continue to
be in full force and effect.

Repeal. All orders, rules and regulations, and other issuances or
parts thereof which are inconsistent with the provisions of this Order, are hereby
repealed or modified accordingly.

Effectivity. This Order shall take effect immediately upon
publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
DONE, in the City of Manila, this 25th
year of Our Lord, Two Thousand and Twenty-Five.
day of October
By the President:
KUCAS P. BERSAMIN
Executive Secretary
